detail:
Decisions: Chose to duplicate the compactor's junk signature in a standalone zero-dependency script rather than have the field repo take a server release — the field project cannot absorb a release right now, and the sanctioned path (twining_housekeeping compact_archives + execute) sweeps the entire live board without the archive:false opt-out that only exists on the unreleased branch; duplication is the lesser evil because the signature is frozen by definition (it matches what the archiver stamped historically, which cannot change retroactively); Chose to preserve blank lines as no-ops and keep every unparseable line verbatim, matching the engine, rather than normalizing files during compaction — the script's only job is removing provably-generated junk, and any other rewrite would make it a data migration that deserves its own review; Tightened the field probe's isLoopJunk to require the detail prefix too, matching the compactor's full seven-field signature — the probe previously checked six fields and would report a junk count slightly higher than the compactor would actually drop, which would read as the repair having silently failed
Findings: Verified the standalone compactor against a fixture with four near-miss entries differing from the signature in exactly one field each (detail text, agent_id, entry_type, scope): all four preserved, along with an unparseable line and a genuine finding. Only true junk dropped, all-junk file deleted, junk-free file left byte-identical (not rewritten), no temp files leaked, preview verified byte-identical, and a second execute is idempotent.; The standalone script and twining_housekeeping({compact_archives:true}) now share the identical seven-field predicate, so a preview from either agrees with the other — worth keeping in sync if the archiver's summary format ever changes (it has been stable across the full git history of archiver.ts).
summary: Added standalone archive compaction script so the #35 repair can run without a server release; aligned probe matcher to the compactor's seven-field signature
